_about: Intentional, audited divergences from the verbatim v1 content. The reference sections (src/content/sections/*.html), the live calculator subsystem (src/ui/calculators-live.mjs) and the framework-chart node files (src/content/nodes/<income>/<marker>.json) are generated from main:v1/flowchart.html and are held byte-identical to it by gates 9, 10 and 8, so a figure that goes stale there cannot be fixed by editing those files. Targets: 'section:<view>', 'calculators-live', 'node:<income>/<marker>' (a node correction applies to its detailsHtml only). Each entry below is applied by tools/build-v2.mjs on top of the verbatim text at build time; tools/verify-corrections.mjs (gate 13) proves every 'find' still matches the verbatim source exactly 'count' times, so a v1 change or a silent drift fails the build. Tokens in 'replace': {{fig:key}} -> the figure's display string, {{figval:key}} -> its raw number. Hand-typed derived numbers carry the derivation in 'reason'. Every entry names the audit claim it corrects and the primary source read on 'verified'.

corrections.find: For 2026, the phase-out begins at $201,775 single / $403,550 MFJ and completes at $276,775 single / $553,550 MFJ (Rev. Proc. 2025-32)
corrections.replace: For 2026, the phase-out begins at {{fig:qbi_sstb_phasein_start}} and completes at {{fig:qbi_sstb_phasein_complete}} (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.26)
corrections.reason: The verbatim v1 node gave $201,775 / $403,550 and $276,775 / $553,550. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.26 gives threshold $201,750 (all other returns) / $403,500 (MFJ) and phase-in range amount $276,750 / $553,500; $201,775 / $276,775 are the married-filing-separately figures and $403,550 / $553,550 appear nowhere in the table. Re-derived: the upper end is the threshold plus the phase-in range of $75,000 ($150,000 joint) that P.L. 119-21 §70105(a) wrote into §199A(b)(3)(B) and (d)(3): 201,750 + 75,000 = 276,750; 403,500 + 150,000 = 553,500. The rest of the sentence (the $50K/$100K to $75K/$150K expansion) matches §70105(a). Also claim CL360.

corrections.find: OBBBA made the $10K SALT cap permanent (with limited phase-in increases for households under $500K AGI), leaving the PTET election
corrections.replace: OBBBA raised the SALT cap to $40,400 for 2026 (rising 1% a year through 2029, then back to $10,000 from 2030), reduced by 30% of modified AGI above $505,000 but not below $10,000, leaving the PTET election
corrections.reason: The verbatim v1 node said OBBBA made the $10K SALT cap permanent. P.L. 119-21 §70120 (new 26 U.S.C. §164(b)(7)) sets the cap at $40,400 for 2026, 101% of the prior year's amount for 2027-2029 and $10,000 from 2030, reduced by 30% of modified AGI above $505,000 (2026) but not below $10,000 (half amounts for married filing separately, not stated on the page). Every number in the replacement is read from the statute; none is derived. The same paragraph's $400K PTET worked example (approximately $13K recovered) is NOT changed: it rests on unstated assumptions (state tax rate, other SALT paid, filing status, modified AGI), so it is flagged to the owner rather than recomputed.

P.L. 119-21 §70413(b) struck $10,000 and inserted $20,000 in the last sentence of 26 U.S.C. §529(e)(3) for taxable years beginning after 2025-12-31. Only the figure is changed. Not added (new content, owner's call): §70413(a) also widened the K-12 expenses that count beyond tuition (curriculum, books, online materials, outside tutoring, test fees, dual enrollment, certain therapies) for distributions after enactment.
